title: WOUND infection and clinical outcomeS IN patients with Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia
summary: Patients with CLTI are at a high risk of amputation and death. Amputation rates increase even further in cases of infected wounds. Currently, there is limited evidence available on the relationship between specific pathogens and limb as well as survival outcomes. Therefore, this multicenter, prospective cohort study aims to investigate the correlation between pathogen patterns and limb and survival outcomes, as well as bloodstream infection rates. The ultimate goal is to identify patients who are at a high risk of amputation. Secondly, we aim to generate appropriate empirical antibiotic regimens and identify patients who would benefit from early antibiotic therapy to reduce the unnecessary use of antibiotics and, consequently, minimize selection pressure on antimicrobial resistance.

interventions.name:
Patients with PAD rutherford category 5 and 6 and:
•	Clinically infected leg ulcers (According to WIfI-classification)
•	Endovascular or surgical treatment for PAD
will, during the hospitalization preceding the index procedure, be interviewed using a structured questionnaire to obtain information

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with PAD rutherford category 5 and 6 and:
•	Clinically infected leg ulcers (According to WIfI-classification)
•	Endovascular or surgical treatment for PAD
Exclusion criteria:
No peripheral ulcers
